lines: I remember having no trade, no thoughts, almost no self. You helped with the important one.
I did not know what I would become, but you made sure I could become anything.
You pulled me back when even my name felt far away.
I remember your voice cutting through the fever.
Food tasted right again this morning. I nearly cried.
I slept without waking <shake>afraid</shake> for the first time.
Thank you for staying when I could not recognize you.
I can walk through the village as myself again.
My hands look familiar now. That still feels like a gift.
You gave me another chance to find where I belong.
I do not know how to repay a life, but I can try to use mine well.
The village bell sounds normal again instead of painfully loud.
I remember who kept watch beside me. I will not forget.
Being alive leaves room to become useful.
I woke hungry for bread instead of anything terrible.
Every ordinary thing feels important after losing all of it.
I am still tired, but it is an honest kind of tired.
You saw a person in me when I could not.
I have pieces of myself back every day.
Whatever work I find next, I will remember who gave me the chance.
Your face is familiar. So is being confused, but this feels different.
I remember waking with empty hands and a head full of broken bells.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
Some names return before the faces that belong to them.
I know this village, but parts of it still look wrong.
Please repeat yourself if I lose the thread.
I remember being <shake>afraid</shake> before I remember why.
There are hours missing, and I do not know if I want them back.
The cure worked. My memory is taking longer.
I knew the path home yesterday and forgot it this morning.
Do not take it personally if I stare. Recognition comes slowly.
Food tastes familiar even when the table does not.
I keep hearing the bell in memories that cannot have a bell.
Tell me what happened plainly. I can handle plain words.
I am trying not to force the pieces into the wrong order.
Your voice is easier to remember than your name.
I know I should be grateful. I am still catching up to why.
Every answer seems to uncover two more questions.
Stay nearby, but give me a moment to think.
I believe you helped me. The rest will come when it comes.
I remember you, though I still do not know what to do with the memory.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Please keep the door open. Closed rooms make it worse.
I woke certain I was still dangerous. Part of me still believes it.
Your kindness is real. So is my need for space.
Some sounds make me think the sickness is back.
I remember the hunger too clearly to laugh about it.
Do not come closer without warning me first.
My hands shake around people I trust. I hate that.
The <shake>fear</shake> lasted longer than the fever.
I am cured, but I do not feel safe inside my own head yet.
Stand where I can see you and we will be alright.
I want to thank you without pretending everything is fixed.
Sometimes I recognize a face and still want to run.
I need fresh air more than company right now.
Help can be real even when trust still hurts.
If I go quiet, give me time instead of questions.
I am not angry with you. I am trying to stay present.
I will get better. Just do not rush me there.
